chapter: New Orleans bands: Cheek, Parker, Morgan
title: Papa Salter's band and money in town versus out
summary: The band doing percentage jobs in New Orleans, its rhythm section, and pay of a few dollars.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Yeah, we call them PC, percentage. Yeah. We had a short name for it, PC. It was all in New Orleans. In New Orleans too? The Papa Salter's great band was doing that. They didn't make no money.
Did they make more money on working the door than they get a cash job?

The Papa Salter's band was so far down one time, I worked with them. I worked with them for a while. Yeah. During the time when he had Adam Kitto, Paul Bobran was here. Paul Bobran was on the drums. The thing was bad. Yeah. Paul was in there. I was in rhythm section. Me, Paul Bobran, Kitto, and Lance Trotter on the drums. Mm-hmm.
Did you make more money going out of town than playing in New Orleans?
Well, it was about the same. You know, you could get some money in circulation, you'd leave. Yeah.
I mean, it wasn't that easy to get jobs in your own and you had to go in there.
Well, you could get a, you know, but the job was then dollar a night. Yeah. Right here.
Well, how much would you make on a percentage job though?
Well, we'd be lucky to come back sometime with eight or ten dollars. Mm-hmm. Twelve dollars was the most. You mean for one night or the weekend? Yeah, one night is on the weekend.
